prompt: Four scatterplots have correlation coefficients $r = 0.85$, $r = -0.92$, $r = 0.15$ and $r = -0.40$. Which one shows the STRONGEST linear relationship?
hint: Strength depends on how close $r$ is to $1$ or $-1$. The sign only tells you the direction of the trend.

hints.text: Strength depends on how close $r$ is to $1$ or $-1$. The sign only tells you the direction of the trend.
Drop the signs and compare the sizes $0.85$, $0.92$, $0.15$ and $0.40$. The largest size belongs to the strongest relationship.
$0.92$ is the largest size, so $r = -0.92$ shows the strongest linear relationship: choice B.

explanation: The correlation $r$ runs from $-1$ to $1$, and values near either end mean the points hug a line tightly.
Because a negative sign only means a downhill trend, compare the sizes without signs: $0.85, 0.92, 0.15, 0.40$.
$0.92$ is the biggest, so $r = -0.92$ describes the strongest linear pattern. That is choice B.

alternativeExplanations.title: Picture each plot
steps: $r = 0.15$: a shapeless blob. $r = -0.40$: a loose downhill cloud.
$r = 0.85$: a fairly tight uphill band. $r = -0.92$: an even tighter downhill band.
Tightest band wins, regardless of up or down.
